First, we factor the polynomial on the left-hand side of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2} & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}+2x-15) \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}-3x+5x-15) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x(x-3)+5(x-3)) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x+5)(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we define the function $f(x)$ as

$$
f(x)={x}^{2}(x+5)(x-3).
$$

So we're now solving the inequality $f(x)\le 0.$

The solutions to the equation $f(x)=0$ are $x=-5,$ $x=0$ and $x=3.$ These roots divide the number line into $4$ subintervals: 

$$
(-\infty ,-5),\,(-5,0),\,(0,3),\,(3,\infty ).
$$

Now, we construct a sign table with the list of the intervals on the top and the list of factors on the left. Filling in the sign table using the usual method, we get the following result:

|  | $(-\infty ,-5)$ | $(-5,0)$ | $(0,3)$ | $(3,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}^{2}$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x+5$ | $-$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x-3$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $f(x)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Finally, to solve the inequality $f(x)\le 0,$ we look at the bottom row to determine where $f(x)$ is negative.

From the table, we see that $f(x)$ is negative on the intervals $(-5,0)$ and $(0,3).$

Therefore, remembering that the roots are also solutions, we conclude that $f(x)\le 0$ for all $x\in [-5,3].$
